newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close up on commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close up on commercial buying.

text.p: Active commercial buying added to early chart support and CME live cattle futures closed higher, traders noted. Feeder cattle futures also ran up for gains in nearbys on short covering sparked by a break in CBOT corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.575 cent per lb higher to unchanged with June up 0.575 at 64.025 cents. Feeder cattle ended mostly 0.750 higher to 0.350 lower with August up 0.700 at 76.750.

Live cattle held chart support early and moved up late as commercial buying increased and touched off buy stops. Somewhat greater-than-expected fed cattle sales volume early Tuesday and ideas cash cattle prices may be near a bottom turned futures up, traders said.

The fact that futures held the 63.250-cent support level and that packers were willing to pay $63 per cwt for fed cattle rather than push hard for $62, despite lower boxed beef values, sparked support in the pit. Lack of delivery notices added to support in June, they said.
Deferred months also posted gains despite expectations Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report is expected by most market watchers to show expanding fed cattle supplies, sources said.

Early analysts' projections put total on-feed cattle supplies in the closely-watched seven-state area between 111.5 and 114 percent of a year ago as of June 1. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates ranged from 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings 97 to 100.5 percent.

Locals and E.D.&F. Man bought June late after selling early. RBH notably bought August and other back months while Dean Witter bought August and Prudential Securities sold. In options, commercials sold 62 puts while commission houses bought August 65 to 68 out of the money calls and sold December 70 puts, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures also turned up as CBOT corn futures broke, with higher live cattle futures reinforcing demand. Technically, the market also held chart support areas between 76.350 and 76.000 cents, which added to gains, they said.
"There is a bull flag on the weekly charts and you had a key reversal up today," said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst at Dean Witter.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.18 at $77.58 per cwt. However, the index is still near its highest level since mid-August, 1994.
With a low in August feeder futures Tuesday of 75.650 cents, futures moved to too large a discount to the index which also prompted support, traders added.
E.D.&F. Man sold August early with R.J. O'Brien and locals buying later but prices took off late when buying by RBH touched off buy stops, pit sources said.
